newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end up on stronger CBOT market.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end up on stronger CBOT market.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher on Tuesday across the board as local investors were encouraged to buy after the Chicago market overnight gained, traders said.
Prices were 40 to 210 yen higher, with the benchmark July 1998 contract up 40 yen at 13,350 yen per tonne. Volume was estimated at 58,127 lots.
The CBOT corn market's price gains, which were triggered by USDA crop reports, encouraged investors to buy, traders said.
On Monday, USDA said U.S. farmers this year seeded 80.2 million acres to corn, below an average of analysts' estimates of 81.8 million.
"In the longer term, the developing El Nino weather pattern will help support the Tokyo corn market," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.47 per bushel at 0745 GMT, down from $2.48 at Monday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $7.67-1/2 a bushel at 0745 GMT, against $7.71 at Monday's close.
